instruction: Write a TypeScript generic identity function identity<T>(value: T): T and show calls with a string and a number.
Write a TypeScript generic class Stack<T> with push, pop, peek and a size getter, throwing on pop of an empty stack.
Write a TypeScript generic function pluck<T, K extends keyof T>(items: T[], key: K): T[K][] that extracts one property from each object.
Write TypeScript code using Partial<T> to update a user record with only the provided fields, in an updateUser function.
Write TypeScript code using Record<K, V> to build a lookup table from an array of {id, label} objects.
Write TypeScript code using Pick<T, K> to create a public view of a User with only id and name, and Omit to strip the password field.
Write TypeScript code using Readonly<T> and ReadonlyArray<T> to define immutable config and ensure push is rejected on the array.
Write a generic TypeScript function firstOf<T>(items: readonly T[]): T | undefined, and a constrained generic filterTruthy<T>(items: T[]): T[] that removes null and undefined.
Write TypeScript code using ReturnType<typeof fn> and Parameters<typeof fn> to type a wrapper around an existing function.
Write a TypeScript generic function memoize<TArgs extends unknown[], TResult>(fn: (...args: TArgs) => TResult) with proper generic typing.
Write TypeScript code using Exclude and Extract to derive subtypes from a union of event names.
Write TypeScript code using Required<T> to force all optional properties of an interface to be present.
Write a TypeScript generic class TypedEmitter<Events extends Record<string, unknown>> with typed on and emit methods.
Write TypeScript code using Array<T> versus T[] syntax and a generic tuple type Pair<T> with a swap function.
Write TypeScript code with a generic constrained to an interface HasId, and a generic uniqueById function returning a Map keyed by id.
Write a TypeScript generic comparator-based sort function and a custom GenericDictionary<K extends string, V> class with get and set.
Write TypeScript code implementing NonNullable<T> manually as a conditional type and using it in a function signature.
Write a TypeScript generic factory createWithDefault<T>(defaults: T, overrides?: Partial<T>): T that merges defaults with overrides.
Write TypeScript code contrasting any with a generic: show an untyped identity function losing type information, then the generic version preserving it.
Write a TypeScript generic deep pick helper using mapped types: type DeepPartial<T> that recursively makes all properties optional.
